facts.statement: The study used a mouse model with postnatal neuronal GPX4 deficiency to investigate its role in traumatic brain injury.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Mice lacking neuronal GPX4 showed worse brain swelling, higher intracranial pressure, and greater blood leakage than control mice after injury.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Giving the drug ferrostatin-1 one and six hours after injury reduced cell death and brain damage in the deficient mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The researchers note that their genetic model starts losing GPX4 early in development, so it does not show the effects of losing the enzyme only in adulthood.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors state that while their results strongly suggest ferroptosis is a key cause of damage, other injury mechanisms might also be involved.
